land.text: the country 'bounded by the Sadanira river in the west, the Kausiki river in the east, the Ganga river in the south' and the Himalayas in the north, 'the northern part of what in present time is the Indian state of [Bihar]' and 'the Tarai region and the south-eastern parts of Nepal' (Videha page); the same polygon as the Vajjika League's country in janapada-of-vajji, which names Videha as its predecessor

successors.note: Infobox 'succeeded by: Vajjika League'; the Vaidehas joined the league 'as one of the two most important members' but 'maintained limited autonomy within the league'. The page dates the end of the monarchy to 'c. 7th century BCE'.

capitals.name: Mithila (Balirajgarh, Madhubani)
capitals.note: 'The capital of the Vaidehas was the city of Mithila' (Videha page); the Mithila page says 'the Balirajgarh fort in the Madhubani district is regarded as the capital of ancient Mithila' and mentions Janakpur (Nepal) as a later capital. The Vayu Purana calls the capital Jayantapura. Coordinates are the district town's (the pages give none).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Videha row; the Vajjika League row of Cliopatria begins in -600 and the sa-01-c dossier names Videha as its predecessor on the same polygon). The page gives no area; the polygon resolves to about 60,000 km2. Rivers as the page gives them: the Sadanira (Gandaki) west, the Kausiki (Kosi) east, the Ganga south, the Himalayas north.

ledger.note: c. 800 BCE: the kingdom of Maha-Videha is founded under King Renu. 'Founded around 800 BCE, according to the Mahagovinda Sutta by the king Renu'. The infobox has 'Established: c. 1100 BCE' and the text 'lasting from around 900 BCE to around 700 BCE' for the monarchy; the Mithila page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mithila_(region)) has 'During the Later Vedic period (c. 1100-500 BCE), Videha became one of the major political and cultural centers'. The year is the Sutta's date as the page gives it; the country is the page's river bounds.

ledger.note: c. 7th century BCE: the Videha monarchy gives way to the Vajjika League. The infobox dates the league's overthrow of the monarchy to 'c. 7th century BCE' and the text says 'around the 7th or 6th century BCE, the Licchavi tribe invaded the territory'; 'This monarchical period of the Vaidehas lasted between 150 and 200 years'. -601 is my bridging year, the year before the Vajjika League dossier's start (-600); the page gives no year.

certainty.note: A kingdom of the Brahmanical and Buddhist texts; the river bounds are the page's, the dates are 'around' dates and the page contradicts itself (c. 1100 or 900 or 800 for the start).

sources.title: Videha
sources.note: Identity, founding around 800 BCE under Renu, monarchy 900-700, Licchavi and Vajjika League, Magadha annexation by 468, bounds by the Sadanira, Kausiki, Ganga and Himalayas, capital Mithila.

sources.title: Mithila (region)
sources.note: Later Vedic period c. 1100-500 BCE; Videha incorporated into the Vajjika League; bounds by the Mahananda, Ganges, Gandaki and Himalayan foothills; Balirajgarh as capital.

notes: The Videha page contradicts itself on the start (infobox c. 1100 BCE; the Mahagovinda Sutta 'around 800'; the monarchy 'around 900 BCE to around 700 BCE'; 'the maximum number of monarchical kings was eight' against a list of fifty-odd Janakas), so the whole life is soft. -800 is the Sutta's date. The ruler strip is not given (the Janaka list is legendary and the page's count is inconsistent). The end -601 is bridging (the year before the league dossier's -600 start): the monarchy ended 'c. 7th century'; between about -700 and -600 the land is the Licchavis' and the Vajjika League's per the page, drawn here as Videha to meet the sa-01-c dossier, which names Videha as the league's predecessor and starts in -600. The polygon is the one sa-01-c uses for the league's country (a fallback form; a gap-filler may replace it with the Gandaki-Kosi band from the gazetteer's river entries). The Kosala page's undated Para Atnara 'ruled over both Maha-Videha and Kosala' is not on a page opened here. The Kingdom of Videha's end in Magadha (468, 'annexed to Magadha') is the Vajji dossier's, not this one's.
